findings.summary: The export passes all projected 1,807,231 rows to one worksheet, exceeding Excel's 1,048,576-row limit by 758,655 rows. EXCEL_MAX_ROWS is never enforced, so the export must fail, truncate data, or produce an invalid/incomplete workbook, violating the downloadability and worksheet-capacity acceptance criteria.

findings.summary: displayedClosing omits supported fx_other consumptions, so the displayed closing balance is overstated by the fx_other total (observed as 1,494,440 TRY) and cannot reconcile exactly.

unverified: No tests are shown covering exact opening/inflow/outflow/conversion/closing turnover and reconciliation for each supported consumption type.
The supplied diff does not show the Pool and sum definitions, so numeric precision, currency-unit handling, and behavior for malformed or missing values cannot be verified.
The diff only computes a closing value; the required display of each turnover component for every pool consumer category cannot be verified from the supplied text.

findings.summary: Each detail amount is rounded independently, so the returned amounts need not sum to the currency-rounded source amount. This violates exact reconciliation and is consistent with the reported 1578 TRY aggregate drift; allocate the rounded remainder deterministically (for example, by largest remainders) so detail cents total exactly to the source cents.
The function neither validates nor normalizes shares, so shares that do not sum to 1 (or are negative/non-finite) can produce an invalid allocation even if rounding residuals are corrected.
Binary floating-point multiplication and Math.round can mis-round decimal currency values near half-cent boundaries; integer minor-unit arithmetic or an explicit decimal-currency strategy is needed.

unverified: No tests are shown for exact cent reconciliation, tie-breaking, negative or zero source amounts, empty shares, non-unit share totals, non-finite inputs, or large values.
The required behavior when the source has more than two decimal places and the deterministic policy for assigning residual cents are unspecified.

findings.summary: The verify script no longer runs `prisma generate`, so schema changes such as `newcrmChangedSince` can be typechecked against stale generated clients, violating the required release-gate ordering.

The `|| echo existing Prisma mismatch` fallback converts every non-zero TypeScript result into a successful script exit, masking genuine type errors and violating the requirement that any typecheck failure remain non-zero.

A temporary reviewer probe is added to the release tree even though the frozen scope permits only product and durable public methodology artifacts and acceptance explicitly excludes temporary reviewer probes.
Private root-cause scratch notes are added to the release tree despite the explicit acceptance requirement that private review scratch notes must not enter it.
